turns.text: real quick, kinda a weird one. its payday so i just set up $150 on venmo to my mom every other friday starting today. she keeps saying shes fine tho

Not weird at all. It sounds like you're wondering whether it's okay to help when she's told you she doesn't need it. What did she say when she said she's fine? Was it a firm no, or more of a brush-off?
more like a brush off lol. she doesnt ask for anything ever. but her hours got cut and i know the math isnt mathing. the mom fund is already in my budget now so its not like i'd miss it

That counts for something. You've built it into your budget, so it won't strain you, and you're sending it steadily, not as a one-off rescue. Plenty of people find a regular, low-key amount easier to accept than a big gesture, because it doesn't ask her to admit anything. Did you send it with a note, or just the money?
just the money and a heart emoji 😮‍💨 she texted back like 10 min later. said its a loan and shes writing it in her notebook. so now idk if i should keep the mom fund going or if im making it weird

That reply tells me quite a bit. She didn't send it back, and she found a way to accept it that lets her keep her pride. Calling it a loan and writing it down is her way of saying yes without feeling like she's taking charity. You don't have to correct her or argue about the word. Whether it's a loan on her notebook page and a gift in your head doesn't change that it helps.

If you want to keep it going, I'd keep it simple and consistent: same amount, same day, no big conversation. If it ever starts to feel heavy for you, that's the moment to adjust it, not before. Want a short, easy text to send back that doesn't turn it into a big thing?

Something like: "Got it 👍 see you in two weeks."

That acknowledges the loan idea without arguing, and it signals the next one is already coming. Easy for her to accept.
